questions.q: What is the real, defining difference between `uint` and `int` in Solidity?
options: They are exactly identical with no real difference
int can never be negative; uint can be positive, negative, or zero
uint can never be negative; int can be positive, negative, or zero
uint is only for strings, int is only for numbers
questions.explain: uint (unsigned integer) is restricted to zero or positive whole numbers, while int (signed integer) can also represent negative values.

questions.q: Why would a developer choose uint8 instead of uint256 for a small value, per this lesson?
options: Smaller uint sizes cost less gas to store than larger ones
There's no real reason — they cost the same
uint256 doesn't actually exist in Solidity
uint8 can hold larger numbers than uint256
questions.explain: The larger the uint size, the more gas it costs to store — so using a smaller size like uint8 for values that will always stay small genuinely saves gas.

questions.q: What is the real default value of an unsigned integer that's declared without being given an initial value?
options: It stays undefined forever
It causes a compile error
Negative one
Zero
questions.explain: The instructor demonstrated live that a uint left without an initial value defaults to zero when you call its getter function.

questions.q: What does msg.sender actually refer to?
options: The Ethereum Foundation's address
The contract's own deployed address
A random address generated on each transaction
The address of the account or contract that called the current function
questions.explain: msg.sender is a global variable that always holds the address of whoever (or whatever) is calling the current function — demonstrated live by switching accounts and redeploying.

questions.q: How many bytes does a Solidity `address` value actually hold?
options: 256 bytes
20 bytes (40 hex characters)
8 bytes
It varies depending on the network
questions.explain: Every Ethereum address is a fixed 20 bytes, represented as 40 hexadecimal characters — the same size for every address on the network.
